analysis:
Examined ClusterSetupLinkExchange.swift base/head and the docs change. Head lines 113-125 add Pairing.Identity, a struct of public values only (localPin, peerPin, clusterID, linkEpoch, edgeID). The edge secret is not included. Head line 172 stores this identity on Responder, and line 184 sets it from pairing.identity. Key derivation is unchanged: edge() at lines 136-146 still keys with ClusterLinkControlKey.qualification(secret, epoch, edgeID). The listener configuration, tag dispatch and size limits at lines 186-223 are unchanged. No secret exposure or auth weakening was found in this file.

The docs at head lines 581-588 describe services answering with the new pairing after re-pairing. They also describe a 'this Mac's pairing changed' log line and restarting an older service that still keeps the earlier pairing.

The ClusterService.swift change (unit 229a758a432fd464:0) had no source text in this batch; only its patch excerpt was visible. That excerpt shows: responder visibility widened from private to internal (line 99); the cable checks renamed to responderCheck/controlCheck with a new Listening dependency (lines 144-147, 168); and changed ranges at head 337-420, likely the pairing-change restart logic. These are unverified.

Integration must check the following in ClusterService:
(1) A pairing change compares Identity and restarts both the exchange listener (port 47422) and the control listener (port 47423, controlLabel).
(2) The old responder is stopped before the new one starts, with no window where both keys are accepted.
(3) Unpairing or forget leaves no listener still answering commands with a forgotten edge secret. Per docs line 612, forget should remove pair cache records and stop the part.
(4) The pairing is re-read from ClusterPairingStore without logging any secret.

No canonical threat ID directly covers the cluster link pairing. This area is outside listed TBs; T-041 is relevant only through the cluster prefix-cache docs, which are unchanged here. Missing ClusterService source limits coverage.
